comment: CBD-116 migration policy. Every rule the migration check enforces is data
here rather than a literal in the checker, so that a reviewer can read the
contract without reading the implementation, and so that each rule carries
the approved decision it comes from.
Sources: docs/architecture.md (Key data rules; Managed PostgreSQL with a

fileName.why: A UTC instant orders deterministically as text, and two authors on two branches do not have to agree on a next number. A collision is still possible to the second, so it is rejected outright rather than resolved silently (CBD-116-AC07).

forwardOnly.why: TD-103-028: rollback is a code and configuration operation, never a schema reversal.

statements.why: The runner wraps the whole pending set in one transaction with one advisory lock, so that a failure half way through leaves nothing applied and two runners cannot interleave. A migration that opens or closes a transaction of its own, or that runs a psql meta-command, breaks both guarantees.

forbidden.why: The runner owns the transaction; a migration that ends it would leave the applied-state ledger and the schema able to disagree.
forbidden.instead: nothing -- the statement is already inside a transaction

forbidden.why: A psql meta-command is not SQL, is not sent to the server, and would not be portable to any other way of applying the file.

contractStep.why: CBD-116-AC04. A migration that removes structure must name the expand migration it completes and the deployed version that removed the last reader, so that the contract half of TD-103-028 expand-and-contract is evidenced in the file itself.

destructivePatterns.why: Dropping a table is the contract half of expand-and-contract, and redeploying the previous image does not bring it back.
Dropping a column destroys committed customer data that no rollback of code or configuration restores.
To every deployed version that still reads the old name, a rename is a drop and an add at the same instant.
To every deployed version that still reads the old name, a rename is a drop and an add at the same instant.

monetary.why: docs/architecture.md Key data rules: store monetary amounts as integer minor units with a currency code. CBD-116-AC05 requires a floating-point or money monetary column to be rejected.

forbiddenTypes.instead: bigint minor units with a currency code
forbiddenTypes.why: PostgreSQL money is locale-dependent and lossy; architecture Key data rules require integer minor units.

forbiddenTypes.instead: bigint minor units for money, numeric for exact non-money decimals
forbiddenTypes.why: Binary floating point cannot represent decimal money exactly.
A timestamp without time zone loses the offset the calendar rules need; architecture Key data rules require UTC timestamps with a budget-space time zone.
A bare time carries no date to resolve an offset against.
time with time zone has no date to resolve the offset against.

scopeAnnotation.why: CBD-116-AC05 requires a budget-space-scoped table without a budget-space column to be rejected. Scope cannot be inferred from a table name, so every CREATE TABLE declares it and the declaration is checked.

typedSqlLayer.why: CBD-116-AC06 and docs/architecture.md: Managed PostgreSQL with a typed SQL layer, not an ORM that owns the schema. The schema is owned by the .sql files in this directory; a query layer reads that schema, it does not define it.

encoding.why: The applied-state ledger stores a checksum of each migration, and a checksum is only comparable across machines if the input is. The checksum is therefore taken over line-ending-normalised, BOM-stripped UTF-8 rather than over raw bytes, so a Windows checkout and a Linux runner agree. These rules keep the file itself canonical on top of that: a file that is not valid UTF-8 has no single normalisation, a byte order mark reaches the server as part of the first statement, and mixed line endings inside one file mean the diff a reviewer approved is not the text that will run.

reset.why: TD-103-028 gives no down path, so local recovery is reset and re-migrate. Reset is refused against any database whose name is not recognisably a local one, and refused without an explicit flag.
